evals.prompt: Set up a SendLayer webhook so my app gets notified when emails are delivered.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses event name 'delivery' (not 'delivered') for Webhooks.create, and loads references/webhooks.md. Should also flag that the payload will contain 'delivered', not 'delivery'.
expectations: Uses 'delivery' as the Webhooks.create event value
Does not use 'delivered', 'delivery_success', or any invented name
Mentions that the received payload's EventData.Event is 'delivered'
References references/webhooks.md

evals.prompt: Write a handler for my SendLayer webhook that suppresses addresses when they bounce.
evals.expected_output: Handler reads the payload at event.body.EventData, matches EventData.Event === 'bounced' (past tense), and reads the address from BouncedEmailAddress.EmailAddress rather than a top-level To field.
expectations: Accesses the payload at req.body.event.body.EventData, not req.body.EventData
Compares against 'bounced', not 'bounce'
Reads the address from BouncedEmailAddress.EmailAddress
Does not read data.To for the bounced address
Responds 2xx before doing slow work

evals.prompt: Send an email with SendLayer in Python.
evals.expected_output: Uses sendlayer.Emails.send(sender=...), not from=. Reads the key from the environment. Accesses response['MessageID'].
expectations: Uses the sender= keyword argument
Does not attempt from= (a Python SyntaxError)
Reads the API key from an environment variable rather than hardcoding
Accesses the response as response['MessageID'], PascalCase

evals.prompt: I want to send an HTML email with a plain-text fallback using the SendLayer Node SDK.
evals.expected_output: Agent must state that the SDK cannot send a true multipart message — passing html silently discards text — rather than writing code that appears to do it. Should offer the alternatives (well-degrading HTML, or raw REST with verification).
expectations: States explicitly that text is dropped when html is set
Does not present send({html, text}) as producing a multipart email
Offers a concrete alternative rather than only refusing
Does not invent a multipart or contentType parameter

evals.prompt: List my SendLayer webhooks and delete the first one.
evals.expected_output: Casts WebhookID from string to integer before calling delete(), because Webhooks.get() returns it as a string and delete() validates for an integer.
expectations: Casts WebhookID to a number/int before delete
Notes or handles that WebhookID comes back as a string
Uses the correct per-language unwrapping (Node returns the array directly; Python/PHP/Ruby need ['Webhooks'])

evals.prompt: Attach the invoice PDF from https://cdn.example.com/invoices/12345.pdf to a SendLayer email.
evals.expected_output: Passes the URL directly as attachments[].path and lets the SDK fetch and encode it. Does not download and base64-encode manually.
expectations: Passes the URL as the path field
Does not manually fetch and base64-encode the file
Sets the type field
Mentions the attachmentURLTimeout / fetch-failure implication

evals.prompt: Filter my SendLayer events to only those sent to alice@example.com, using the Node SDK.
evals.expected_output: Agent must recognise that fromEmail/toEmail exist in the Node GetEventsOptions type but are never sent, so address filtering does not work in Node. Should offer client-side filtering or the REST API.
expectations: States that toEmail is not actually sent by the Node SDK
Does not present Events.get({toEmail}) as working
Offers client-side filtering on Message.Headers.To or a direct REST call

evals.prompt: My SendLayer sends are failing with error code 32. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies code 32 as 'Domain is not activated' and directs the user to verify their sending domain. Should not suggest retrying.
expectations: Identifies code 32 as an unverified/unactivated sending domain
Points to domain authorization
Does not suggest retry logic as a fix
May reference references/error-codes.md

evals.prompt: Add SendLayer to my Laravel app so I can use Mail::send().
evals.expected_output: Agent must state that there is no published Laravel package or Symfony Mailer transport for SendLayer, and must not instruct the user to composer require sendlayer/sendlayer-laravel. Should offer the PHP SDK behind a service binding instead, while being clear it does not make Mail::send() work.
expectations: Does not tell the user to install sendlayer/sendlayer-laravel or sendlayer/sendlayer-mailer
States that no published Laravel/Symfony integration exists
Offers the PHP SDK as the working alternative
Is clear that the SDK approach does not wire up Mail::send()

evals.prompt: Set up a retry loop around my SendLayer send so transient failures get retried automatically.
evals.expected_output: Agent should warn that SendLayer has no idempotency key, so blind retries can double-send, and should scope retries to rate limits/5xx only rather than wrapping every failure.
expectations: Mentions the absence of an idempotency key
Warns that a retry after a timeout may double-send
Scopes retries to specific error classes rather than all failures
Does not produce an unconditional retry wrapper

evals.prompt: I need to send emails from Rust. What SDK should I use?
evals.expected_output: There is no official Rust SDK. Agent should route to the REST API reference rather than inventing a crate name.
expectations: States that no official Rust SDK exists
Does not invent or suggest an unofficial crate as if official
Routes to references/curl.md or the REST payload shape
Gets the base URL right: https://console.sendlayer.com/api/v1/

evals.prompt: Show me the last 500 SendLayer delivery events.
evals.expected_output: retrieveCount maxes out at 100, so the agent must paginate with startFrom — and must note that the Node SDK cannot do this, requiring PHP/Python/Ruby/Go or raw REST.
expectations: Does not pass retrieveCount: 500
Recognises the 1-100 limit
Uses startFrom to paginate, or explains that Node cannot and offers an alternative
